body:
"""The corrective chunk's function reading: the three grown upstream functions against upstream's own score, and the
fork's own functions in their three files against the cognitive ceiling.

usage: python3 fn_scores.py [--acc-bar N]
Tool: rust-code-analysis-cli (the audit's tool, `bars.py`'s recipe: every `function` space, cognitive `sum`).
Upstream's text is read at 547d7514b (the 2026-11-19 sync's merge base, pinned by sha), never by blame.
A function of a file is the fork's own when its name is no function name of that file's upstream text.

Prints one line per function read, then `fn scores: PASS` or `fn scores: FAIL`. PASS when:
- handle_key_or_input_event reads exactly upstream's score (46), compute_presentational_hints exactly 167, and
  build_accessibility_node at most --acc-bar (default 19, upstream's score);
- no fork-own function in the three files reads over 15.
Reads the working tree; builds nothing.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys

UPSTREAM = '547d7514ba2adb357d41d5e4655a63ddd5cdc5ec'
FILES = {
    'packages/blitz-dom/src/accessibility.rs': 'build_accessibility_node',
    'packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs': 'handle_key_or_input_event',
    'packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo/presentational_hints.rs': 'compute_presentational_hints',
}
CEILING = 15

acc_bar = 19
if '--acc-bar' in sys.argv:
    acc_bar = int(sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--acc-bar') + 1])


def functions(path, text=None):
    args = ['rust-code-analysis-cli', '-m', '-O', 'json']
    if text is None:
        out = subprocess.run(args + ['-p', path], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    else:
        # rust-code-analysis-cli reads a file; hand it upstream's text through a temporary path
        import os
        import tempfile
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = os.path.join(d, os.path.basename(path))
            with open(p, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
                f.write(text)
            out = subprocess.run(args + ['-p', p], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    found = []
    stack = [json.loads(out)]
    while stack:
        s = stack.pop()
        if s['kind'] == 'function':
            found.append((s['name'], s['start_line'], s['metrics']['cognitive']['sum']))
        stack.extend(s.get('spaces', []))
    return found


ok = True
for path, grown in FILES.items():
    upstream_text = subprocess.run(['git', 'show', f'{UPSTREAM}:{path}'], capture_output=True, text=True,
                                   check=True).stdout
    upstream = functions(path, upstream_text)
    upstream_names = {name for name, _, _ in upstream}
    want = next(c for name, _, c in upstream if name == grown)
    head = functions(path)
    got = next(c for name, _, c in head if name == grown)
    holds = got <= acc_bar if grown == 'build_accessibility_node' else got == want
    bar = f'<= {acc_bar}' if grown == 'build_accessibility_node' else f'== {want:g}'
    print(f'grown {grown} {path}: {got:g} (upstream {want:g}, bar {bar}) {"ok" if holds else "FAIL"}')
    ok &= holds
    for name, line, cog in sorted(head, key=lambda x: x[1]):
        if name in upstream_names:
            continue
        over = cog > CEILING
        print(f'  fork-own {name} {path}:{line}: {cog:g}{" FAIL over 15" if over else ""}')
        ok &= not over
print('fn scores: PASS' if ok else 'fn scores: FAIL')
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

Since 2026-10-14-quality-gates the `coverage` leg (`bash .github/scripts/ci-leg.sh coverage`, cargo-llvm-cov) ends with per-crate line floors — escher-driver 97 %, dioxus-native-dom 83 %, blitz-test-harness 90 %, by `.github/scripts/coverage_floor.py`, both coverage runs excluding dioxus-native-dom's crate-private `keyboard_compat.rs` (upstream's temporary keyboard-types bridge) until escher takes upstream's retirement of it, the floors unchanged by the exclusion (a `*_tests.rs` `#[path]` test-child file is no record of the per-crate reading, so a test module moved out of line moves its crate's reading with no line of code changed: since 2026-10-19-test-splits escher-driver read 4266/4350 = 98.07 %, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint, which added lint.rs, 4634/4732 = 97.93 %, since 2026-10-20-load-wait 4695/4794 = 97.93 %, and read now under the same floors it reads 4959/5058 = 98.04 % (dioxus-native-dom 2937/3387 = 86.71 %, blitz-test-harness 999/1040 = 96.06 %, as read at CI#42371051720's `Coverage report` job; with `actions.rs`, `check_target`, `actionable_nodes` and `Readings` in the tree CI#42493052318's `Coverage report` check passes under the same floors, the per-crate figures not read), the 97 % floor holding, 3 of 3 crates still at or above their floors) — and the stand checks hold a zero-failure flakiness budget (`ci-leg.sh stand-repeat`: the `stand_*.rs` files, the seventeen named blitz-tests targets of its `--test` list and seven_guis' eight process checks, three rounds, no retry). Since 2026-10-16-fast-failing-mutants a mutation run (dev host only, never in CI — cargo-mutants 27.1.0 and cargo-nextest 0.9.146 are host tools) is cargo-mutants `--test-tool nextest --baseline=skip` under the root `.config/nextest.toml`'s `mutants` profile (`NEXTEST_PROFILE=mutants`: fail-fast at one failure, terminated immediately, the default profile untouched), each unit's test command (`NEXTEST_PROFILE=mutants cargo nextest run --locked`, a `-p` per package, then `--lib` and its `--test=` targets) first read green on the unmutated tree — never under plain `cargo test`, which runs the hung blitz-tests integration binaries before the library tests and reads their mutants `timeout`; a run scoped to one function anchors its filter on the mutant name's verb — the replace verb, then the function's name and a space (the filter is an unanchored regex over the whole mutant name, so a bare function name matches others holding it) — and its mutant listing is read first and must show exactly the mutants the run is meant to test. The Epoch 5 code audit's cognitive-complexity ceiling of 15 is read on the dev host alone (rust-code-analysis-cli 0.0.25, a host tool; no CI leg runs it and it binds no function, engine functions over it left as they are, a fork addition to an upstream function over it going into a function of escher's own with one call in upstream's body, bar the engine's click handler, held below it, upstream's arms included, at the price of a hand re-apply when an upstream sync edits one of its arms), test functions counted — a closure or a nested `fn` keeps its branches counted in its enclosing function, so only splitting a function into module-level sibling items lowers its reading. Upstream's cdp-server and vibey-script duplicated test pairs are kept as upstream wrote them, the duplication reading not held against them.

body: a `url` update re-resolves two `syn` edges into a lock that does not build: the committed lock holds `url` 2.5.9 and `form_urlencoded` 1.2.3 with the `syn` edges of `bindgen` 0.73.2 and `cssparser-macros` 0.7.1 kept at 3.0.6 by edit (the operator's ruling «Keep syn edges (Recommended)» at implement), a state `cargo update -p url` does not produce; on the base lock `cargo update -p url` — alone, `--precise 2.5.9`, or beside `-p form_urlencoded` — moves both edges to `syn` 2.0.119, and `bindgen` 0.73.2, whose `prettyplease` 0.3.0 stays on `syn` 3.0.6, then fails to compile (E0277, `syn::file::File: syn::parse_quote::ParseQuote`); `cargo update -p log` and `-p regex` move no `syn` edge, and a whole `cargo update` moves every `syn 3` edge to 3.0.10 (its build unmeasured). Reproduce: `cargo update -p url --precise 2.5.9 && git diff -U0 Cargo.lock` (two `- "syn 3.0.6", + "syn 2.0.119",` pairs), then `cargo build --workspace --locked`. Any later url update, an upstream sync's lock take included, re-breaks the build until `bindgen` and `prettyplease` agree on `syn`; held as a residual on the operator's wrap directive (chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/inputs/I6-epoch2-corrective-wrap-directive-2026-11-22.md.txt point 3; chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/inputs/I5-relay-1.md.txt; the measurement chunks/2026-11-22-epoch-2-corrective/evidence/url-lock-move.diff)
